report.message: Hi, my vase arrived broken this morning. The box looked fine from outside but the vase is in several pieces. Order #1001, photo attached. Can you send a new one?

evidenceNotes: white ceramic vase shattered into many fragments inside open cardboard box
crumpled brown packing paper visible around fragments
box flaps open, handwritten label with tracking number on inner flap

reasons: Colissimo (La Poste) excludes compensation when the packaging is unsuitable for the content, and the photos show inadequate packaging.

sources.title: Colissimo Entreprise general terms, Contrat Facilite (edition of 2020-12-08; clauses on standard indemnity and 12-month limitation read)
French Commercial Code, art. L133-3 (3-day protest after receipt, carrier liability)

figures.label: Indemnity per kg (standard offers)
figures.note: Read in the 2020-12-08 edition. The 2026 general terms are not public, so the current figure is not confirmed.

figures.label: Cap per parcel (standard offers)
figures.note: Same edition as above. Applies to parcels over 1 kg; up to 1 kg the indemnity is 23 EUR/kg prorated by weight.

figures.label: Domicile with signature: 33 EUR/kg, cap 990 EUR
Time limit to claim
figures.value: 12 months from the day after pick-up (France)
figures.note: Modelled as 365 days counted from the order creation date, because the order has no pick-up date; this is earlier than the real deadline, so it errs on the safe side.

figures.label: Reserve window after delivery
figures.note: L133-3 itself was read, but we could not confirm that it applies to Colissimo parcels (postal regime). The Colissimo general terms set no such deadline. Applied as a warning only, never as a hard block.

notes: UNVERIFIED: the 3-day reserve window (L133-3) is applied to Colissimo out of prudence only; no official text confirms it for La Poste parcels. It never blocks a claim, it only adds a warning.

DATED SOURCE: the amounts (23 EUR/kg, 690 EUR, 33 EUR/kg, 990 EUR) and the 12-month limit come from the 2020-12-08 edition of the general terms; the 2026 edition is not public. Ask the merchant's Colissimo adviser for the current contract.

Colissimo pays the purchase value of the content (supplier invoice), or 70% of the sale value without one. The order only carries the sale price, so the ceiling computed here uses the sale price and the real indemnity may be lower.

No indemnity when the packaging is unsuitable for the content, and no indirect damage. Shipping fees are refunded only for a total loss. Only the weight measured by La Poste counts; the order's declared weight is used here.
The ad valorem option (up to 1000 or 5000 EUR) replaces the standard indemnity and is not modelled; the order does not say whether it was bought. A high-value parcel must go to a human.
Claims are filed by the merchant in the Colissimo Box tracking tool (OSC); no claim API was found.
